accepted.s: Which institution operates the Indian Tsunami Early Warning System and the Ocean State Forecast service in India?
o: National Institute of Ocean Technology, Chennai
Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, Hyderabad
accepted.x: INCOIS, Hyderabad, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, operates ITEWS and provides Ocean State Forecast services.
accepted.tq: Use the institution–function association and distinguish INCOIS from IMD and NIOT.
accepted.sec: Coastal hazard forecasting - Indian institutions → early-warning systems (tsunami, high waves, coastal risk)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the services provided by INCOIS:
1. It provides Potential Fishing Zone advisories.
2. It issues swell-surge, marine heatwave and small-vessel alerts.
3. It operates the SAMUDRA application.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: INCOIS provides PFZ advisories, several marine hazard alerts and the SAMUDRA app; all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check each service against the institution before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Coastal hazard forecasting - Indian institutions → early-warning systems (tsunami, high waves, coastal risk)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning System functions as a UNESCO regional tsunami service provider for how many Indian Ocean countries?

accepted.s: Within approximately what time can the Indian Tsunami Early Warning System issue a warning?
accepted.x: ITEWS is designed to issue tsunami warnings within 10 minutes.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise warning-time figure rather than a general description of rapid warning.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the Indian Tsunami Early Warning System?

accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated monitoring chain rather than choosing a related environmental instrument.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a rip current?
o: A tidal current flowing only towards the beach
A broad current flowing parallel to the coastline
A deep-ocean current caused exclusively by salinity differences
A narrow, fast channel flowing away from the shore
accepted.x: A rip current is a narrow and fast-moving channel of water flowing away from the shore.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the exact direction and form of a rip current from other coastal currents.
accepted.sec: Coastal hazard forecasting - Indian institutions → early-warning systems (tsunami, high waves, coastal risk)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which organisation sanctioned a project using artificial intelligence and satellite tools to detect rip currents for beach safety?
accepted.x: ISRO sanctioned the project using AI and satellite tools for rip-current detection and beach safety.
accepted.tq: Apply the who-developed or who-sanctioned trap to distinguish the space agency from ocean agencies.

accepted.s: In the positive phase of the Indian Ocean Dipole, which of the following conditions generally occurs?
o: The Arabian Sea is warmer and the region south of Indonesia is cooler.
The Arabian Sea and the region south of Indonesia become equally cool.
The Arabian Sea is cooler and the region south of Indonesia is warmer.
Both poles of the Indian Ocean become equally warm.
accepted.x: During a positive IOD, the western pole near the Arabian Sea is warmer while the eastern pole south of Indonesia is cooler.
accepted.tq: Compare the west and east poles before considering the monsoon consequence.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean Dipole - positive vs negative phases and monsoon link  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Ocean Dipole:
1. Positive IOD is associated with more rainfall over India.
2. Negative IOD is associated with less rainfall over India.
3. In the negative phase, the western Arabian Sea is cooler than the eastern pole.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Positive IOD generally brings more rain over India; negative IOD brings less rain, with the Arabian Sea cooler and the eastern pole warmer. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Test the phase, temperature contrast and monsoon effect together rather than memorising one isolated pair.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean Dipole - positive vs negative phases and monsoon link  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Indian Ocean Dipole generally develops during which months and reaches its peak in which month?
accepted.x: The IOD develops in April–May in the equatorial Indian Ocean and peaks in October.
accepted.tq: Retain the development window and peak month as a sequence.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean Dipole - positive vs negative phases and monsoon link  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best describes the relationship between the Indian Ocean Dipole and ENSO?
o: The IOD and ENSO are identical phenomena occurring in different oceans.
The IOD is always caused by ENSO and cannot occur independently.
A negative IOD always offsets La Nina.
The IOD runs independently of ENSO, and a positive IOD can offset an El Nino.
accepted.x: The IOD can develop independently of ENSO; a positive IOD may offset the effects of El Nino, as observed in 1997.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute words such as “always” and distinguish two coupled-ocean climate phenomena.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean Dipole - positive vs negative phases and monsoon link  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Madden–Julian Oscillation is correct?
o: It is a westward-moving belt of clouds beginning over the Pacific Ocean and recurring every 5–10 days.
It is a seasonal reversal of winds confined to the Arabian Sea.
It is an eastward-moving belt of clouds and rain beginning over the tropical Indian Ocean and recurring every 30–60 days.
It is a stationary pressure belt over the subtropical Atlantic Ocean.
accepted.x: The MJO is an eastward-moving belt of clouds and rain that starts over the tropical Indian Ocean and recurs every 30–60 days.
accepted.tq: Combine movement, place of origin and recurrence interval to identify the exact phenomenon.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean Dipole - positive vs negative phases and monsoon link  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Madden and Julian identified the oscillation named after them during
accepted.x: Madden and Julian identified the MJO in 1971–72.
accepted.tq: Use the close decade options to test precise historical recall.

o: INCOIS — second Coastal Flood Monitoring System at Kollam harbour

NASA — SAMUDRA app for Indian fishermen

accepted.s: Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich tracked which phenomenon regarded as an early signal of El Nino?
o: An eastward Kelvin wave carrying warm water along the equatorial Pacific
A southward-moving polar air mass over the Pacific
A westward cold-water surge across the Indian Ocean
A stationary cold eddy in the North Atlantic
accepted.x: The satellite tracked an eastward Kelvin wave, meaning warm water moving east along the equatorial Pacific, an early El Nino signal.
accepted.tq: Identify the signal by combining direction, water temperature and ocean basin.

accepted.s: What proportion of excess warming heat is absorbed by the oceans, according to the stated estimate?
accepted.x: The oceans absorb more than 90% of the excess warming heat.
accepted.tq: Use the inequality sign and percentage range carefully; “more than” is significant.

accepted.s: According to the stated May 2026 warning, a developing super El Nino could have what effect on the 2026 South-West Monsoon?
o: It could strengthen it throughout India.
It could reverse it into a winter monsoon.
It would have no possible effect.
accepted.x: The IMD warned that a developing super El Nino could weaken the 2026 South-West Monsoon.
accepted.tq: Trace the climate-driver and monsoon-effect relationship without assuming every El Nino impact is strengthening.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding El Nino and Bay of Bengal cyclones is correct?
o: El Nino may increase only January–March cyclones in the Bay of Bengal.
El Nino may reduce post-monsoon cyclones in the Bay of Bengal during October–December.
El Nino has no possible relationship with post-monsoon cyclones.
El Nino always eliminates all cyclones in the Bay of Bengal.
accepted.x: An INCOIS study found that El Nino may reduce post-monsoon cyclones in the Bay of Bengal during October–December; the statement does not imply that all cyclones are eliminated.
accepted.tq: Beware of the absolute trap in “always” and retain the specified October–December period.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about low-pressure systems over the Bay of Bengal:
1. There are about 13–14 such systems each year.
2. Most of them form in the northern Bay of Bengal.
3. They can flood the Godavari and Krishna basins.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: About 13–14 Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems form annually; most originate in the northern Bay and can cause flooding in the Godavari–Krishna basins.
accepted.tq: Combine the annual count, formation region and Andhra Pradesh basin impact.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich tracked an eastward Kelvin wave
B. INCOIS installed a second Coastal Flood Monitoring System at Kollam harbour
C. IMD warned of a developing super El Nino affecting the 2026 monsoon
D. INCOIS reported a possible reduction in post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclones due to El Nino
accepted.x: The events occurred in the order: Kelvin-wave tracking on 4 June 2026, Kollam monitoring installation on 14 May 2026, the May 4 monsoon warning, and the July 7 cyclone study. However, by the dates stated, the correct chronological order is C, B, A, D.
accepted.tq: Use the exact dates rather than the order in which the developments are described.
